name: Analog Devices, Inc.
blurb: Analog Devices is one of the two largest analog semiconductor companies in the world (alongside Texas Instruments), with deep expertise in signal-chain ICs, data converters, and — critical for AI servers — power-management products including hot-swap controllers, multiphase voltage regulators, power-system management ICs (PSMICs), and DC-DC power stages. ADI's LTC4284/4286/4287 hot-swap family protects 48V AI rack infrastructure, while its MAX20790 and related multiphase controllers regulate power to GPUs and accelerators at the point-of-load. The company is also a leading supplier of 800 VDC first-stage conversion solutions designed to NVIDIA's high-voltage DC reference architecture for AI factories.
recent: ADI reported Q1 FY2026 (quarter ending January 2026) EPS of $2.46 versus the $2.31 consensus, with revenue of $3.16 billion supported by a 50% year-over-year increase in data-centre revenue. AI and data-centre exposure now accounts for roughly one-fifth of total revenues. Q2 FY2026 guidance was set at $3.5 billion (±$100 million), with non-GAAP EPS of $2.88 (±$0.15) and adjusted operating margin of ~47.5%. In August 2025 ADI announced its first 800 VDC hot-swap and first-stage power solutions targeting NVIDIA intelligent platform management, with >98% conversion efficiency. The company has seen accelerating adoption of 48V/54V intermediate-bus converters and smart power stages for vertical power delivery in AI racks.
